recipes.about:
Make a little room for Christmas with a three-day paper calendar.

Choose from six themes:
• Bible readings — daily passages in WEB or BSB.
• Holiday movies — a movie pick and an original movie-night prompt.
• Christmas mystery — a family-friendly clue each day, with the answer on Christmas.
• Acts of Kindness — a practical, thoughtful way to help someone each day.
• Daily Self-Affirmations — gentle reminders for holiday calm, self-compassion, and joy without excess.
• Christmas Around the World trivia — a sourced question and answer about a festive tradition each day.

The five December themes begin December 1; Bible readings begin on the first Sunday of Advent. Future mystery clues stay sealed until their date. All four layouts and daily content are included. Dates follow your TRMNL account time zone. QR codes open Bible passages or the day's movie on Rotten Tomatoes. The other themes have no QR codes.

Missed a day? Visit Geolizard.com/advent for today's entry and earlier items, updated daily after each theme's countdown starts. All entries remain available through December 31; the website resets for the next year on January 1.

Your interests, one important visual story. An off-device AI editor ranks recent stories from a bounded set of official sports, tech, AI, gaming, Tesla, creator and NASA feeds. Source images or video previews lead; original headlines, attribution and dates stay visible. A thumbnail is not necessarily an event frame. New or unreviewed stories use a labeled freshness fallback. Not comprehensive world news or a live video player. Public preference fields travel in URLs and may appear in hosting logs. No viewer API key required.

See the current positions of all eight planets around the Sun, updated hourly. Compare their distances in AU, kilometres, or miles, and locate the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The diagram uses a simplified scale to keep every planet visible.

Displays a random question from the 118 questions in the Discover Canada study guide for the Canadian citizenship test. Questions marked with a ★ are official test questions. Data Source.
Some questions ask about your own Head of State, MP, Premier or Mayor. Fill in the fields below and your answers replace the placeholder text in the static data.
Arithmetic practice for kids age 5-11 (selectable).

recipes.d: Trade plans grid, pushed by webhook
recipes.about:
Trade Plan Board shows a clean grid of trading plans on your TRMNL: ticker, status, reference price, entry, stop, targets with optional R multiples, and a short invalidation line.

The full screen holds up to six plans in a 3-by-2 grid, or 2-by-3 in portrait. Half horizontal shows 2 plans on TRMNL OG and 3 on TRMNL X. Half vertical shows up to 2 stacked. Quadrant shows a single plan. The title bar reads Trade Plans. The preview on this page uses invented demo tickers and round numbers only, never live positions.

This is a webhook recipe. After you install it, copy your unique URL from the Webhook URL field on this plugin's settings page (a click-to-copy field) and POST JSON to it. Put every field inside a merge_variables object. A push replaces the stored data. Each installer pushes their own data; the author's feed is never shared. Leave "Share pushed data with installs" off.

Using Grok Bot? Ask it for a routine that POSTs your data to the Webhook URL above on a schedule — no code needed.

Payload schema. Top-level keys:
• plans (required) — an array of plan objects. The full layout shows the first 6; mashup sizes show fewer.
• grid_cols and grid_rows (optional) — kept for compatibility. The markup chooses columns from the layout and orientation.
• empty_slots (optional) — extra empty cells on the full layout only, for a fixed 3-by-2 when you have fewer than 6 plans.
• note (optional) — title-bar instance text, for example Demo data.

Each item in plans:
• ticker — short symbol, for example ACME
• status_short — short status, for example WAIT, ARMED, or OPEN
• ref_price — shown with a $ prefix
• flag — optional extra label; omit or leave blank to hide it
• entry_zone and stop — shown with a $ prefix

recipes.d: A book passage for every minute
recipes.about:
A stylized literary clock. For every minute, it shows a passage from a book that names that very minute, set as a typographic poster: the words that tell the time large and black, the story around them sized so every line runs edge to edge, the book and its author in the title bar.

A passage for each of the 1440 minutes of the day, nearly all with a real time phrase ("twenty minutes past seven"), and where possible one that fits the half of the day, so evenings get evening scenes. The quotes come from public-domain books on Project Gutenberg and the literature-clock collections of JohsEnevoldsen (CC BY-NC-SA 2.5), cdmoro and utrost (AGPL-3.0).

Made by ExcuseMi.

recipes.about:
A rotary phone rings. A radio murmurs by the window. Steam rises from a freshly opened rice cooker. Kurashi brings the small rituals of Showa Japan to your TRMNL, one illustrated object at a time.

Kurashi means everyday life. This collection pairs sixty original ink illustrations with short Japanese stories and separately sourced historical notes. Its printed-book layout gives each object room to breathe.

The cards are in Japanese; setup is in English. Optional furigana and a short English gloss are available in settings. Choose a new object each day, a new object at each refresh, or keep a favorite on display. Seasonal modes follow your TRMNL time zone. Full-screen and all three mashup layouts are included, with shorter selections on smaller screens.

No extra account, API key, or additional service setup is needed. Artwork and fonts are hosted for you. Historical references accompany the full-screen cards; the illustrations and stories are period-inspired interpretations.

recipes.d: Home value from Zillow ZIP data
recipes.about:
Estimates your home's value from what you paid and how typical home values in your ZIP code have changed since, using the Zillow Home Value Index (updated monthly).

Enter your ZIP code, and optionally your purchase price and the month you bought. The plugin shows today's estimated value, your gain in dollars and percent, the typical home value in your ZIP, and how much values there have changed over the last 12 months. Leave the purchase fields blank to show the typical home value for any ZIP code. You can also show your street address or a nickname as the heading; it stays in your plugin settings and is never sent to the data server.

There is no sign-up or API key. The estimate follows typical homes in your ZIP, not your specific house, so it is not a Zestimate or an appraisal. Data: Zillow Research. Questions and issues are welcome on GitHub.

recipes.d: See where the Earth runs hot
recipes.about:
Ever wonder which volcanoes are running hot right now? Hotspots gives you a global view.

Hotspots turns NASA satellite observations of thermal activity into a minimalist map of the world's volcanoes.

Each known volcano gets its own little marker, sized according to the relative thermal activity detected by satellites.

Hotspots also checks the Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program for reported ongoing eruptions. Volcanoes listed as erupting get a little ash plume, so you can tell them apart from volcanoes showing a heat signal alone.

As observations age, the markers fade, so you can see where activity has been spotted recently without drowning in data.

Install (don''t Fork!) to receive future updates.

recipes.d: A window into the deep ocean
recipes.about:
A window into the abyss.
Turn your TRMNL into your personal window into the deep ocean. Abyss lets you peek into a fascinating corner of our planet: the deep Pacific. Explore hydrothermal vents on Axial Seamount, a methane seep at Southern Hydrate Ridge, and the Oregon Offshore seafloor. These are real research camera images from places most of us will never visit.

Choose your view
Cycle through all four cameras, choose a few favourites, or settle into one. Leave the camera selection empty to rotate through every published camera.

The default 15-minute refresh rotates your selected views. Images are processed every three hours from periodic recordings and snapshots. When a camera cannot update, its last good image stays on display.

Where are the cameras?
Four camera views across three research sites in the northeast Pacific. Both vent cameras are on Axial Seamount; the other cameras look across Southern Hydrate Ridge and the Oregon Offshore seafloor. All depths are approximate.

ASHES: Mushroom vent — about 1,540 m
On Axial Seamount, an active underwater volcano on the Juan de Fuca Ridge. This camera looks into the ASHES hydrothermal vent field, where hot fluids emerge from the volcanic seafloor.
Explore the research site · Detailed site map

International District: Tiny Towers — about 1,520 m
A second hydrothermal vent field on Axial Seamount. The Tiny Towers camera offers another view of the volcano's deep-sea habitat.
Explore the research site ·

Setup

2. Fill in your organization name: the part after appsignal.com/ in the address bar when you open AppSignal. Leave App blank to see every app, or enter one app's name.
3. Save, and add the plugin to a playlist.

To see example data without connecting, enter demo as the organization.
